title: Beef Stew with Potatoes, Puerto Rican Style

content.title: About
content.content: Beef stew with potatoes Puerto Rican style is a classic island dish where beef is slowly braised with aromatic spices, tomato sauce, olive oil, olives, capers, and chunks of potato. The stew has a rich, slightly sweet flavor with hints of garlic, oregano, and vinegar.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: In Puerto Rico the stew is often cooked in clay pots (cazuelas), which impart a unique earthy aroma.
Traditional recipes include a “adobo” blend of vinegar, garlic, oregano, and olive oil.
Potatoes are cut into large cubes so they hold their shape and absorb the sauce.
The dish is commonly served with rice, beans, and fried plantains.
Locally it is known as “Carne Guisada” and is a staple for holidays and family gatherings.

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Beef provides complete protein essential for muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Iron and zinc
items.content: Red meat supplies easily absorbed iron and zinc, supporting immunity and energy metabolism.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The stew delivers B12, B6, and niacin, important for nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Potassium from potatoes
items.content: Potatoes add potassium, which helps regulate blood pressure.

items.title: Antioxidants from spices
items.content: Garlic, oregano, and vinegar contain antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Beef can be high in saturated fat; choose lean cuts if you have cardiovascular concerns.

items.title: Salt and sauce
items.content: The stew often contains added salt and soy‑based sauces, which may raise blood pressure.

items.title: Spice allergies
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to garlic, oregano, or olives.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Because of meat, oil, and potatoes, the dish is calorie‑dense; portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stew hot, typically alongside white rice, beans, or fried plantains. A squeeze of lime or fresh cilantro adds brightness.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Cool the stew to room temperature, then store in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3 days. For longer storage, portion into freezer‑safe containers and freeze up to 2 months. Reheat thoroughly before serving.
